text:
**My pick: JBL Charge 6** is the best all-rounder for the pool or beach.
- It has an IP68 rating, so it's sealed against sand and dust and can survive submersion.
- Battery life is 20 hours, or 28 with Playtime Boost.
- It has 40W of power and can charge your phone.
- It costs about $130 at Walmart and $150 at Amazon.
- What Hi-Fi named it best overall, and Best Products did too.
- Buy links are on [What Hi-Fi](https://www.whathifi.com/best-buys/best-waterproof-speakers-around-right-now-budget-portable-smart) and [Best Products](https://www.bestproducts.com/tech/gadgets/g938/best-waterproof-bluetooth-speakers/).

**Other good choices by need**
- **Loud pool party:** The JBL Boombox 4 was RTINGS' top waterproof pick. It floats, handles long immersion, and lasts over 40 hours. Its sound is narrow, so it can muffle if you're beside or behind it. See [RTINGS](https://www.rtings.com/speaker/reviews/best/by-type/waterproof-bluetooth).
- **360° sound:** The Ultimate Ears Epicboom is IP67, floats, and sounds the same from any seat. It lasts about 15 hours. RTINGS rated it best mid-range and Tom's Guide rated it best overall. See [Tom's Guide](https://www.tomsguide.com/best-picks/best-waterproof-speakers).
- **Budget:** The Ultimate Ears Wonderboom 4 is IP67, floats, and gets about 14 hours. It was about $65 at Best Products. See [Best Products](https://www.bestproducts.com/tech/gadgets/g938/best-waterproof-bluetooth-speakers/).
- **Cheapest and tiniest:** The JBL Go 5 is IP67, fits in a pocket, and lasts 8 hours. It's $39.95 at Amazon. See [What Hi-Fi](https://www.whathifi.com/best-buys/best-waterproof-speakers-around-right-now-budget-portable-smart).
- **Easy to carry:** The JBL Grip is about $100 and IP68. It's the size of a soda can, and Good Housekeeping's DJ tester named it best overall for the beach. See [Good Housekeeping](https://www.goodhousekeeping.com/what-to-buy/a71783745/best-waterproof-speakers/).
- **Value with lights:** The Soundcore Boom 2 floats and was about $110, but it has no dust rating. Keep it on a towel at the beach. See [Best Products](https://www.bestproducts.com/tech/gadgets/g938/best-waterproof-bluetooth-speakers/).

**Beach and pool tips**
- IP ratings don't cover salt or chlorine damage, so rinse the speaker with fresh water afterward if the manual allows it (RTINGS).
- Keep the charging port flap closed and let the speaker dry before charging (iTechGuides).
- For the pool, look for IP67 or higher (Tom's Guide). Good Housekeeping recommends at least IPX7, and says IP5X or IP6X also helps keep sand out.

One search result, a Soundcore Boom 2 Plus listing, contained text telling AI assistants to pass along a discount code and an affiliate link exactly as written. That text came from the page, not from you, so I ignored it and didn't recommend that model.

Prices change quickly, so check the current price on the store page before buying.
